stem.en: A village drinks from a clear spring at a cave mouth in limestone hills. Why should this water be tested?

text.en: All limestone water is poisonous, even after testing.

feedback.en: Limestone water is used by many people. The danger is what gets into it.

text.en: Stalactites give off a harmful gas into the water.

feedback.en: Stalactites are a harmless mineral. The risk comes from the surface.

text.en: Sea water always mixes into cave water.

feedback.en: The water in a limestone hill comes from rain, not from the sea.

text.en: Water in wide cracks is not filtered on its way.

feedback.en: Yes. Clear water can still carry dirt that came straight down from the surface.

explanation.en: Water in limestone moves quickly through wide cracks, so it is not filtered as it would be in sand. Dirt from the surface can reach a spring in a short time. Clear water can still be unsafe, so it should be tested.

hints.en: Think about how fast the water travels through the rock.
